title: A person’s life
prompt: Describe a real or imaginary friend or family member. Say where they were born, where they grew up, one past event and what they like doing now.
checks: I used was born and a past event.
I used a family word correctly.
I used like + -ing.
I can use an imaginary person instead of sharing private details.

title: Plans and possibilities
prompt: Describe an imaginary school-holiday project. Say what you have decided to do, what you predict or hope, and how you will help someone.
checks: I used going to for an existing plan.
I used will for a prediction or offer.
I included a place and a time.
My predictions are presented as ideas, not certain facts.

title: A surprising afternoon
prompt: Write an original short story about a misplaced object. Describe what two people were doing, an event that interrupted them, and what happened next.
checks: I used was/were + -ing.
I used a past simple action with when or while.
I included house or furniture words.
The story has a clear ending.

title: A route and an arrangement
prompt: Invent a small town. Give directions from its station to a meeting place, then describe an arrangement with a friend for next week.
checks: I used at least three direction phrases.
I used a/an for a first mention and the where appropriate.
I used present continuous for an agreed future plan.
My route is fictional and clear.

title: A message with recent news
prompt: Write an imaginary message about a project or holiday. Include two things you have done, something you have never done, a recent event with just, and one finished event with a past time.
checks: I used have/has + past participle.
I included never and just.
I used past simple with a finished time.
I asked my reader a question.

title: A character and a club
prompt: Invent a character joining a school club. Describe the person, a small problem with a lost object, two club rules, and a polite refusal or changed plan.
checks: I used two phrasal verbs.
I distinguished mustn’t from don’t have to.
I included a polite social reply.
I described fictional club rules clearly.
